paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God makes the promise, and God keeps the promise. He opens with "I am God Almighty" (Genesis 17:1), and then He says "I will establish My covenant" (Genesis 17:2). Look at who is doing the establishing. Abraham is ninety-nine and is lying facedown in the dirt, and God is the One building the whole thing.

That's why Abraham's laugh matters. He asks himself, "Can a child be born to a man who is a hundred years old?" (Genesis 17:17). I think he's looking at his own math, and the math says no. God answers anyway: "Your wife Sarah will indeed bear you a son" (Genesis 17:19). His promise doesn't wait on what we can work out. When your numbers say no, God's Word still gets the last say.

So what's left for us? Trust Him and do what He says, and do it that very day, the way Abraham did (Genesis 17:23). The sign was Abraham's part, but the promise was always God's. Notice He didn't forget the son Abraham spoke up for, either: "As for Ishmael, I have heard you" (Genesis 17:20). He hears you too, baker. Walk before Him and let Him do the establishing.
